r66_01.label: RATES_US_TREASURY_VS_STIR_SWAP_SPREAD_PROXY
r66_01.distinctness_ruling: NOT a renamed curve spread. A curve spread trades two points on one issuer's own curve and cannot change sign; a Treasury-versus-short-rate spread trades government against collateralised/interbank funding at a matched point and HAS gone negative post-2008. Verified at source: r43/rv.py:81-98 declares 24 rates structures and not one pairs a US Treasury future with a US short-rate future.

gate_a.why_no_re_parameterisation: For a single linear hedge the maximum achievable variance reduction IS the regression R-squared, 0.1058. No beta, no window and no estimator can reach the 0.25 floor with SR3 as the hedge leg, so a second window would be searching for a number the data cannot produce.
gate_a.economic_reason: ZN carries about 6.5 years of duration; SR3 is a 3-month rate future whose daily volatility is 27x smaller. The empirical return beta (median 15.4) is not a DV01 match and subtracting it ADDS variance.
gate_a.what_it_would_have_been_if_measured: the HUMAN_GATED unconditional long-ZN book wearing a hedge as a disguise - which the director named in advance as the exact risk this gate exists to catch.

r66_01.independent_confirmation_from_feasibilit: The same structure needs 1 ZN : 17 SR3 - eighteen contracts, $4,203,247 of gross notional, 42.4x the entire NAV. The statistical failure and the feasibility failure have the same cause.

data_blockers_named_exactly.THE_DEEPER_CAPABILITY_LIMIT: A genuine fixed-income hedge is a DV01 hedge. DV01 needs duration, which needs either the swap curve or the bond and contract analytics. The estate owns neither, so it can only hedge like-for-like points on the same curve where an empirical return beta happens to approximate the DV01 ratio. Gate A is the measured proof of that limit.
